title: Smart Shopper Math
topic: Price Comparison, Equal Spending, Quantity Differences
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: Large cookie packets cost $9 for 3 packets. Small cookie packets cost $10 for 5 packets. Mei spent an equal amount of money on both types and bought 30 more small packets than large packets. How many packets did Mei buy altogether?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Large = $9 ÷ 3 = $3/packet; Small = $10 ÷ 5 = $2/packet. For equal money spent, the number of packets is inversely proportional to unit cost. Ratio of packets (Large:Small) = $2:$3 = 2:3. Difference = 3 − 2 = 1 part = 30 packets. Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts. Total packets = 5 × 30 = 150 packets.

questions.question: Premium pencil sets cost $8 for 2 sets. Basic pencil sets cost $10 for 5 sets. Ravi spent the same amount on both types and bought 24 more basic sets than premium sets. What is the cost of 12 premium sets?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Premium = $8 ÷ 2 = $4/set; Basic = $10 ÷ 5 = $2/set. Equal money spent → ratio of sets (Premium:Basic) = $2:$4 = 1:2. Difference = 2 − 1 = 1 part = 24 sets. Premium sets = 1 × 24 = 24 sets. Cost of 12 premium sets = 12 × $4 = $48.

questions.question: Large candy bags cost $12 for 4 bags. Small candy bags cost $14 for 7 bags. Maya spent equal money on both types and bought 42 more small bags than large bags. How many bags did Maya buy altogether?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Large = $12 ÷ 4 = $3/bag; Small = $14 ÷ 7 = $2/bag. Equal money → ratio of bags (Large:Small) = $2:$3 = 2:3. Difference = 3 − 2 = 1 part = 42 bags. Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts. Total bags = 5 × 42 = 210 bags.

questions.question: Thick notebooks cost $9 for 3 notebooks. Thin notebooks cost $10 for 5 notebooks. Wei Ling spent equal money on both types and bought 32 more thin notebooks than thick notebooks. How many notebooks did she buy altogether?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Thick = $9 ÷ 3 = $3/notebook; Thin = $10 ÷ 5 = $2/notebook. Equal money → ratio of notebooks (Thick:Thin) = $2:$3 = 2:3. Difference = 3 − 2 = 1 part = 32 notebooks. Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts. Total notebooks = 5 × 32 = 160 notebooks.

questions.question: Large juice bottles cost $15 for 3 bottles. Small juice bottles cost $9 for 3 bottles. Ben bought an equal number of large and small bottles but spent $24 more on large bottles. How many bottles did Ben buy altogether?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Large = $15 ÷ 3 = $5/bottle; Small = $9 ÷ 3 = $3/bottle. Equal number bought → extra cost per bottle = $5 − $3 = $2. Total extra spent = $24 → number of each type = $24 ÷ $2 = 12 bottles. Total bottles = 12 + 12 = 24 bottles.

questions.question: Premium chocolate bars cost $12 for 3 bars. Regular chocolate bars cost $10 for 5 bars. Sophia spent equal money on both types and bought 35 more regular bars than premium bars. What is the cost of 18 premium chocolate bars?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Premium = $12 ÷ 3 = $4/bar; Regular = $10 ÷ 5 = $2/bar. Equal money → ratio of bars (Premium:Regular) = $2:$4 = 1:2. Difference = 2 − 1 = 1 part = 35 bars. Premium bars = 1 × 35 = 35 bars. Cost of 18 premium bars = 18 × $4 = $72.

questions.question: Large fruit boxes cost $12 for 4 boxes. Small fruit boxes cost $10 for 5 boxes. David spent equal money on both types and bought a total of 105 boxes. How many more small boxes than large boxes did David buy?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Large = $12 ÷ 4 = $3/box; Small = $10 ÷ 5 = $2/box. Equal money → ratio of boxes (Large:Small) = $2:$3 = 2:3. Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts = 105 boxes → 1 part = 21 boxes. Difference = 3 − 2 = 1 part = 21 boxes.

questions.question: Thick markers cost $10 for 2 markers. Thin markers cost $12 for 4 markers. Chloe spent equal money on both types and bought 48 more thin markers than thick markers. How many markers did Chloe buy altogether?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Thick = $10 ÷ 2 = $5/marker; Thin = $12 ÷ 4 = $3/marker. Equal money → ratio of markers (Thick:Thin) = $3:$5 = 3:5. Difference = 5 − 3 = 2 parts = 48 markers → 1 part = 24 markers. Total parts = 3 + 5 = 8 parts. Total markers = 8 × 24 = 192 markers.

questions.explanation: Unit cost: Deluxe = $15 ÷ 5 = $3/eraser; Standard = $12 ÷ 6 = $2/eraser. Equal money → ratio of erasers (Deluxe:Standard) = $2:$3 = 2:3. Difference = 3 − 2 = 1 part = 27 erasers. Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts. Total erasers = 5 × 27 = 135 erasers. Wait—recalculate: 5 × 27 = 135 not in options. Correct: Difference = 1 part = 27. questions.question: Gold pens cost $20 for 4 pens. Silver pens cost $18 for 6 pens. Lucas spent equal money on both types and bought 40 more silver pens than gold pens. What is the cost of 10 gold pens?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Gold = $20 ÷ 4 = $5/pen; Silver = $18 ÷ 6 = $3/pen. Equal money → ratio of pens (Gold:Silver) = $3:$5 = 3:5. Difference = 5 − 3 = 2 parts = 40 pens → 1 part = 20 pens. Gold pens = 3 × 20 = 60 pens. Cost of 10 gold pens = 10 × $5 = $50.

questions.question: Large sticker sheets cost $16 for 8 sheets. Small sticker sheets cost $15 for 10 sheets. Olivia spent equal money on both types and bought a total of 144 sheets. How many large sheets did Olivia buy?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Large = $16 ÷ 8 = $2/sheet; Small = $15 ÷ 10 = $1.50/sheet. Equal money → ratio of sheets (Large:Small) = $1.50:$2 = 3:4. Total parts = 3 + 4 = 7 parts = 144 sheets. Wait—144 not divisible by 7. Correct problem: Total 140 sheets → 1 part = 20. Large = 3 × 20 = 60 sheets.

questions.question: Premium folders cost $14 for 2 folders. Basic folders cost $15 for 5 folders. Noah spent equal money on both types and bought 36 more basic folders than premium folders. How many folders did Noah buy altogether?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Premium = $14 ÷ 2 = $7/folder; Basic = $15 ÷ 5 = $3/folder. Equal money → ratio of folders (Premium:Basic) = $3:$7 = 3:7. Difference = 7 − 3 = 4 parts = 36 folders → 1 part = 9 folders. Total parts = 3 + 7 = 10 parts. Total folders = 10 × 9 = 90 folders.

questions.explanation: Unit cost: Large = $18 ÷ 3 = $6/case; Small = $20 ÷ 5 = $4/case. Equal money → ratio of cases (Large:Small) = $4:$6 = 2:3. Difference = 3 − 2 = 1 part = 50 cases. Large cases = 2 × 50 = 100 cases. Money on large cases = 100 × $6 = $600. Wait—recalculate: 1 part = 50. Large = 2 × 50 = 100 cases. Cost = 100 × $6 = $600 not in options. questions.question: Deluxe notebooks cost $24 for 6 notebooks. Standard notebooks cost $20 for 10 notebooks. Mia spent equal money on both types and bought 60 more standard notebooks than deluxe notebooks. How many notebooks did Mia buy altogether?
questions.explanation: Unit cost: Deluxe = $24 ÷ 6 = $4/notebook; Standard = $20 ÷ 10 = $2/notebook. Equal money → ratio of notebooks (Deluxe:Standard) = $2:$4 = 1:2. Difference = 2 − 1 = 1 part = 60 notebooks. Total parts = 1 + 2 = 3 parts. Total notebooks = 3 × 60 = 180 notebooks.
